T1_insurance_pricing.description: Fair, robust, sustainable EV insurance pricing for Malaysia
T1_insurance_pricing.core_challenge: Limited historical claims data, battery-specific risks, geographic factors

evidence.claim: EV insurance premiums 10-30% higher than comparable petrol vehicles
evidence.implication: Pricing reflects real cost differential, but adequacy unknown

evidence.claim: Battery represents 30-50% of vehicle value
evidence.implication: Concentrated value risk, total loss threshold lower for EVs

evidence.claim: Current EV pricing uses ICE-based models with unknown adequacy
evidence.implication: Actuarial data gap, need Malaysian-specific claims data

evidence.claim: Motor segment underwriting loss RM289.3M, combined ratio 103%
evidence.implication: Industry-wide pricing pressure, EV exacerbates existing challenges

evidence.claim: ADAS sensors drive up repair costs (front-end damage cascades)
evidence.implication: Technology risk underpriced, calibration costs RM5k-15k per incident

evidence.claim: EV depreciation 6-14% faster than petrol vehicles
evidence.implication: Sum insured volatility, betterment calculations complex

evidence.claim: Geographic risk factors: flood-prone areas need separate consideration
evidence.implication: Location-based pricing needed, <20% have flood cover

data_gaps: No published Malaysian EV claims frequency data
No severity benchmarks by damage type

T2_customer_solutions.description: Innovative, customer-centric insurance solutions for EV landscape
T2_customer_solutions.core_challenge: New technologies, changing usage patterns, charging behaviours, evolving customer needs

evidence.claim: 76% of ASEAN-6 respondents plan EV purchase within 5 years
evidence.implication: Massive addressable market for EV insurance products

evidence.claim: Zurich Z-Driver EV Protect: RM120 add-on covers battery, charger, cable
evidence.implication: Affordable bundled solution, market validation

evidence.claim: Great Eastern GREAT EV: battery replacement allowance, wall charger RM10k
evidence.implication: Competing products emerging, differentiation possible

evidence.claim: <20% of EV owners have special perils (flood) add-on
evidence.implication: Critical coverage gap, educational opportunity

evidence.claim: Home wallbox and charging cable not covered by standard motor policy
evidence.implication: New product components needed, customer awareness low

evidence.claim: Cross-border charging corridor exists (Singapore-Thailand)
evidence.implication: Travel insurance integration opportunity

evidence.claim: Takaful options emerging (Zurich Z-Driver Takaful)
evidence.implication: Shariah-compliant products needed for Malaysia market

T3_ecosystem_resilience.description: Strategic solutions for long-term resilience, sustainability, scalability of Malaysia's EV ecosystem
T3_ecosystem_resilience.core_challenge: Repair costs, charging infrastructure gaps, systemic risks, coordinated risk management

evidence.claim: Charging infrastructure at 56% of 2025 target (5,624 of 10,000)
evidence.implication: Infrastructure gap constrains adoption, regional inequality

evidence.claim: DC fast chargers exceeded target (128%), AC chargers at 40%
evidence.implication: Highway coverage improving, urban/residential coverage lagging

evidence.claim: Charger-to-vehicle ratio worsening (1:16, up from 1:13)
evidence.implication: Infrastructure not keeping pace with adoption

evidence.claim: 7 of 10 independent workshops decline EV repairs
evidence.implication: Repair ecosystem bottleneck, after-sales support gap

evidence.claim: 870,000 batteries need recycling by 2050
evidence.implication: End-of-life management critical, pre-treatment capacity only

evidence.claim: Malaysia only has pre-treatment capacity for battery recycling
evidence.implication: Black powder exported, post-treatment infrastructure needed

evidence.claim: MS 2818 Battery Passport launched (ASEAN first)
evidence.implication: Digital traceability framework established, implementation ongoing

evidence.claim: Second-life batteries: 30-50% lower capital cost, 70-80% CO2 reduction
evidence.implication: Circular economy opportunity, PV-ESS integration viable

evidence.claim: Fuel subsidies reduce EV cost advantage for 90% of users
evidence.implication: Policy barrier to adoption, BUDI95 mechanism insulates consumers

evidence.claim: Malaysia trails ASEAN peers (3-5.5% vs Singapore 45%, Thailand 18-21%)
evidence.implication: Competitive disadvantage, policy recalibration needed

evidence.claim: Localization shift: CKD incentives until 2027, CBU restrictions tightening
evidence.implication: Industry restructuring, supply chain localization

structural_constraints: Total loss frequency higher than ICE

cross_track_insights.pricing_to_ecosystem: Insurance pricing must reflect ecosystem realities: repair costs, infrastructure gaps, total loss dynamics
cross_track_insights.customer_to_pricing: Customer demand for bundled solutions (battery, charger, flood) creates product design opportunities
cross_track_insights.ecosystem_to_customer: Infrastructure and repair ecosystem maturity directly impacts customer experience and insurance claims
cross_track_insights.sustainability_to_pricing: Battery lifecycle management (second-life, recycling) affects long-term insurance cost structures

strongly_supported: Malaysia's EV market doubled in 2025 with 44,813 registrations
Charging infrastructure at 56% of government target
EV insurance premiums 10-30% higher than ICE vehicles
Repair ecosystem immature with limited certified workshops
Malaysia trails regional peers in EV adoption
conflicting_uncertain: CBU tax expiry impact on 2026 momentum (some say continues, others predict slowdown)
True EV penetration rate (MAA vs JPJ data discrepancy)
Battery lifespan (8-10 years traditional vs longer for LFP)
Total loss frequency (anecdotal vs systematic data pending)
